page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmgn6i.24xlarge is an x86_64 bare-metal GPU-accelerated server instance within the ecs.ebmgn6i family. The system features 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8163 processors, paired with 384 GB of system RAM at a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration is provided by four NVIDIA T4 GPUs, contributing a combined total of 64 GB of GDDR6 VRAM across the system.

Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 30 Gbps, operating via KVM-based infrastructure. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage or external data volumes for persistent filesystems and application data. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided by default.

The combination of four NVIDIA T4 GPUs and high dedicated core density delivers cost-efficient throughput for parallel computing tasks compared to higher-tier enterprise accelerator platforms. The primary architectural trade-off is the reliance on external storage arrays for high-throughput disk operations, alongside the lack of integrated NVMe drives.

This hardware profile is tailored for distributed deep learning inference, video transcoding and decoding pipelines, computer vision processing, and moderate machine learning model training workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmgn6i.24xlarge is an x86_64 bare-metal GPU-accelerated instance from the ecs.ebmgn6i family. Powered by Intel Xeon 8163 processors, it provides 96 dedicated vCPUs and 384 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The server integrates four NVIDIA T4 GPUs offering 64 GB of aggregate VRAM. Networking features a 30 Gbps baseline bandwidth under KVM hypervisor architecture. The platform does not bundle onboard local storage, necessitating reliance on remote storage solutions. This configuration balances multi-GPU hardware acceleration with dense CPU compute, providing cost efficiency for scale-out parallel workflows. It is suitable for deep learning inference, batch video transcode pipelines, computer vision models, and GPU-driven distributed data processing.
